title: A fly whole-brain spiking model built from BANC or the male CNS keeps the validated sugar-to-MN9 and grooming predictions, not the bitter-versus-Ir94e difference; BANC loses screen accuracy
abstract: Question: do the experimentally validated predictions of the Shiu et al. 2024 whole-brain leaky integrate-and-fire model of the fly (built from FlyWire) stay correct when the same model is built from two other adult fly connectomes? Approach: we used our validated re-implementation of the model, built it from FlyWire v783, BANC v888 and the male CNS v1.0 with raw synapse counts, a global gain matched to FlyWire input synapse counts (BANC x1.69, male CNS x0.57) or a per-cell-type gain, and scored it against the published experiments: an optogenetic screen of 106 feeding-region cell types, nine taste-interaction results, Johnston's-organ input to the aBN1 grooming neuron and ten named sugar-pathway neurons. Results: our FlyWire model reproduced the published MN9 rates (r = 0.997). Screen AUROC at 50 Hz was 0.84 in FlyWire, 0.79 in the male CNS (difference -0.05, p = 0.054) and 0.62-0.72 in BANC (p = 0.004-0.046); true positives 9, 8 and 3-6 of 13. Sugar input drove the contralateral MN9 more than the ipsilateral MN9, JO-CE but not JO-F input drove aBN1, and 8-9 of 10 named neurons responded as observed in all maps without runaway activity. The bitter-versus-Ir94e difference (bitter abolishes the response to strong sugar, Ir94e does not) did not transfer: bitter suppression was too weak in BANC (0.56-0.59 vs 0.07 in FlyWire, through the same inhibitory cell types) and both inputs abolished it in the brain-only male CNS. Side-specific incomplete sensory axons and runaway loops in the nerve cord and antennal lobe limited transfer. Limitations: model results only, three individuals of two sexes and three reconstruction methods, so biological and technical differences are not separated; sugar and water neurons outside FlyWire were assigned by connectivity.
